_about: Maize problems recognised by the VLM, named as in ICAR-IIMR publications. key_signs are short field-identification cues drawn from ICAR-IIMR bulletins (Maize Diseases and their Management 2024; Major Diseases of Maize 2018; Insect Pests of Maize 2024; FAW bulletins) and are used by the second-check vision model. Advice/chemicals are NOT stored here: they come from the verified MaizeGPT table pests_diseases.json.

problems.name: Maydis leaf blight (MLB)
problems.key_signs: Small oval to diamond-shaped tan lesions that elongate between veins into rectangular, brown lesions with darker margins; lesions merge into irregular patches; scorched look in severe cases.

problems.name: Turcicum leaf blight (TLB)
problems.key_signs: Long (2.5-15 cm) elliptical, cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions, not limited by veins, starting on lower leaves; favoured by cool humid weather.

problems.name: Banded leaf and sheath blight (BLSB)
problems.key_signs: Water-soaked straw-coloured lesions on basal leaf sheaths with alternating dark-brown bands, spreading upward; dark brown sclerotia on sheaths, husks and cobs.

problems.name: Charcoal rot (post-flowering stalk rot)
problems.key_signs: After flowering under water stress: premature drying of upper leaves, soft compressible lower stalk; split stalk shows shredded pith with minute black microsclerotia giving a charcoal-grey colour.

problems.name: Fusarium stalk rot (post-flowering stalk rot)
problems.key_signs: Wilting with dull grey-green leaves after flowering; lower stalk turns straw-coloured; split stalk shows soft decayed pith with light pink to tan discoloration (not black specks).

problems.name: Bacterial stalk rot
problems.key_signs: Water-soaked, soft rot of basal internodes and sheaths, stalk looks boiled, characteristic foul fermenting odour; plants topple from the 2nd-3rd internode, often during rainy hot weather before/around tasselling.

problems.name: Pythium stalk rot
problems.key_signs: Soft, water-soaked, collapsed first internode above soil, plants fall over but stay green for a while; no foul odour.

problems.name: Common rust
problems.key_signs: Raised, powdery, cinnamon-brown elongated pustules scattered on BOTH leaf surfaces.

problems.name: Polysora (southern) rust
problems.key_signs: Small, round, orange to light-brown pustules densely clustered mainly on the UPPER leaf surface; favoured by warm humid weather.

problems.name: Grey leaf spot
problems.key_signs: Narrow, rectangular, grey to tan lesions strictly bounded by leaf veins, parallel to veins, with sharp straight edges.

problems.name: Downy mildew (sorghum / brown stripe / Rajasthan)
problems.key_signs: Chlorotic yellow-white stripes or half-leaf chlorosis on young plants, white downy growth on leaf underside in humid mornings; stunting, malformed tassel; brown stripe type has narrow chlorotic-to-reddish stripes.

problems.name: Common smut
problems.key_signs: Swollen silvery-white galls on ears, tassels or stalks that burst to release black powdery spores.

problems.name: Head smut
problems.key_signs: Tassel and/or ear replaced by a mass of black spores with thread-like vascular strands; leafy proliferation of tassel.

problems.name: Ear/cob rot (Fusarium, Aspergillus)
problems.key_signs: Pink-white (Fusarium) or green-yellow powdery (Aspergillus, aflatoxin risk) mould on kernels, often starting at the tip or insect-damaged kernels.

problems.name: Curvularia leaf spot
problems.key_signs: Small round to oval spots with light centre and dark brown margin surrounded by a yellow halo.

problems.name: Phaeosphaeria leaf spot
problems.key_signs: Small round to oval pale-green to bleached spots with dark brown margins, scattered on leaves.

problems.name: Bacterial leaf streak
problems.key_signs: Narrow tan to brown streaks between veins with wavy (not straight) margins and yellow halo when backlit.

problems.name: Viral disease (mosaic / chlorotic stripe)
problems.key_signs: Mosaic or fine chlorotic streaks/stripes on young leaves, stunting; often linked to aphid or leafhopper vectors.

problems.name: Fall armyworm
problems.key_signs: Window-pane scraping on young leaves, ragged holes, wet sawdust-like frass in the whorl; larva with inverted-Y on head and four dark spots in a square on the 8th abdominal segment; egg masses covered with buff hairs.

problems.name: Spotted stem borer (Chilo partellus)
problems.key_signs: Rows of small shot holes on unfolding leaves, dead heart in young plants, tunnels in stalk with frass; larva creamy with dark spots in rows.

problems.name: Pink stem borer (Sesamia inferens)
problems.key_signs: Pinkish larva without spots tunnelling the stalk, oblong holes on leaves, dead heart; common in rabi maize.

problems.name: Shoot fly
problems.key_signs: Dead heart in seedlings (central shoot dries and pulls out easily, rotten smell at base) within the first month; no holes on leaves.

problems.name: Maize aphid
problems.key_signs: Colonies of small soft blue-green insects on tassel, whorl or leaf undersides, honeydew and sooty mould.

problems.name: Thrips
problems.key_signs: Silvery or whitish streaks and specks on leaves, curling, tiny slender insects in the whorl, mostly in dry weather.

problems.name: Termite
problems.key_signs: Wilting and lodging, roots and lower stalk eaten and filled with soil, white soft-bodied insects in tunnels; worse in dry sandy soils.

problems.name: Cob borer / earworm (Helicoverpa armigera)
problems.key_signs: Larva feeding on silk and kernels at the cob tip, frass inside husk; larva striped, variable colour.

problems.name: Other leaf-feeding caterpillars (armyworm, cutworm)
problems.key_signs: Leaves eaten from margins or seedlings cut at ground level; caterpillar without the fall armyworm head/abdomen markings.

problems.name: Nitrogen deficiency
problems.key_signs: Yellowing of OLDER (lower) leaves starting at the tip and moving along the midrib in a V-shape; pale stunted plants.

problems.name: Phosphorus deficiency
problems.key_signs: Purple to reddish-purple colour on leaves and stems of young plants, dark green older leaves, stunting.

problems.name: Potassium deficiency
problems.key_signs: Yellowing and scorching (browning) of the MARGINS of older leaves while the centre stays green; weak stalks.

problems.name: Zinc deficiency
problems.key_signs: Broad pale-yellow to white bands on either side of the midrib on YOUNG leaves (white bud), midrib and margins stay green; short internodes.

problems.name: Healthy maize (no visible problem)
problems.key_signs: Uniform green leaves without lesions, pustules, stripes, holes, insects or discoloration.
